title: festuca arundinacea subsp. conferta
intro: Festuca arundinacea subsp. conferta, commonly known as Sheeps' Fescue or Buffalo Grass, is a perennial grass native to New Zealand. It is a type of grass that has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties and has been found to have various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which can aid in wound healing and reduce inflammation. The therapeutic actions of Festuca arundinacea subsp. conferta include antioxidant, anti-cancer, and anti-diabetic properties, which can help protect against cell damage and support overall health. The bioactive constituents of this plant include sesquiterpenes, phenolic compounds, and flavonoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and health benefits.
